USD.catalyst: The dollar index (DXY) is testing support around 101.51 after slipping below its 20-day moving average of 101.89, pressured by retreating Treasury yields and a sharp equity rout centered on technology shares. Market expectations for Federal Reserve policy have softened, with fed funds futures pricing a 22% probability that the FOMC will refrain from delivering further rate increases this year. The currency trades down 0.91% across its G10 composite over the past week as yield differentials narrow against European and Antipodean peers. The near-term macro focus shifts directly to preliminary October S&P Global PMIs due today and September housing data ahead of the FOMC's October 27–28 policy decision.

GBP.catalyst: Sterling maintains positive weekly momentum across G10 crosses, gaining 0.09% over the past seven sessions after September headline inflation accelerated to 3.5% year-on-year, touching its highest level since October 2025. Markets have nearly fully priced a 25-basis-point interest rate increase by the Bank of England at its upcoming November 5 Monetary Policy Committee meeting. The currency trades above its 20-day moving average of 1.3268 against the greenback while confronting technical resistance near the 50-day average at 1.3408. Domestic attention now turns to upcoming UK retail sales figures to test consumer resilience under elevated borrowing costs.

EUR.catalyst: The euro remains subdued near multi-month lows, with CFTC data showing leveraged funds expanding net short exposure to -92,833 contracts as of the week ending October 13, sitting in the 4th percentile of the 52-week distribution. ECB Executive Board member Fabio Panetta noted ahead of next week's policy gathering that rising yields represent a drag on growth rather than a systemic crisis, while French 10-year yields have touched their highest levels since 2002. Against the dollar, the single currency is capped below its descending 20-day moving average of 1.1248 and 50-day moving average of 1.1447. Markets are split ahead of the October 28 Governing Council meeting, where forecasters such as MUFG anticipate an immediate pause before potential rate hikes later in the cycle.

JPY.catalyst: The Japanese yen has caught strong haven bids, rising 0.8% against the dollar toward 156.86 amid an equity selloff driven by artificial intelligence valuation concerns and broad risk aversion. Domestic fundamentals have reinforced the currency, as Japan's September core CPI accelerated unexpectedly to 2.2% year-on-year against 1.4% consensus, while ex-fresh food and energy inflation reached 2.4% against 1.8% expected, reviving expectations of a higher Bank of Japan terminal rate. The move lower in USD/JPY has broken below both the 20-day moving average of 157.89 and the 200-day moving average of 158.54 via a wide-range bar. Traders are closely monitoring the Bank of Japan's impending policy meeting on October 28–29 for signals on quantitative tightening and rate trajectory following earlier hikes toward 1.25%.

AUD.catalyst: The Australian dollar trades with modest composite gains of +0.66% over the past week, supported by hawkish Reserve Bank of Australia expectations despite softer domestic flash PMIs indicating private-sector contraction for the first time in five months. Market pricing reflects persistent core price pressures that keep an RBA rate increase in play for the upcoming November meeting. Against the dollar, the currency has pushed above its 20-day moving average of 0.6979, testing resistance near its 200-day moving average of 0.7053. Traders await third-quarter Australian CPI data next week as the definitive hurdle for RBA policy expectations.

CAD.catalyst: The Canadian dollar has posted a composite 1-week gain of 0.58% across G10 peers, drawing support from firm energy markets as WTI crude holds above $100 per barrel. Domestic input costs surprised to the upside with Canada's September PPI rising 2.0% month-on-month against 1.3% prior, though earlier September labor market job losses have clouded the growth backdrop. Against the greenback, the loonie has pushed the cross down through its 20-day moving average of 1.4182 toward the 50-day moving average at 1.4007. The immediate focus rests on Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem and the upcoming BoC rate decision scheduled for October 28.

CHF.catalyst: The Swiss franc trades marginally lower on the session, down 0.20% across G10 composites today and 0.06% on a one-week horizon, as the Swiss National Bank indicated that readiness for foreign exchange interventions has eased while noting the franc's carry-trade appeal. Spot USD/CHF has settled near 0.8202, holding beneath its 20-day moving average of 0.8296 while finding support above the 50-day average of 0.8191. Bilateral flows against European peers remain buoyed by widening sovereign yield spreads and fiscal stress in French government bonds. The domestic calendar is light until Monday, when the SNB is scheduled to publish its latest monetary policy and banking statistics.

NZD.catalyst: The New Zealand dollar is outperforming across G10 peers today, posting a composite gain of +0.26% on the session and +0.53% over the week. Third-quarter domestic inflation slowed to 3.7% year-on-year, but underlying price breadth and sticky non-tradable inflation have firmed expectations for policy tightening. Analysts at ASB have warned that an RBNZ hold would sharply weigh on the kiwi given that markets are positioned for a potential hike. Against the dollar, the currency has established support above its 20-day moving average of 0.5635, with all eyes on the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's official cash rate decision scheduled for October 28.

NOK.catalyst: The Norwegian krone leads the G10 complex over the past week with a composite gain of 1.55%, propelled by a substantial terms-of-trade dividend as WTI crude oil trades above $100.40 per barrel. Macro support is underpinned by Norges Bank maintaining its policy rate at 4.50%, generating a wide weekly performance spread of 2.437% against the euro. Against the greenback, spot USD/NOK has dropped below its 20-day moving average of 9.512 and 200-day moving average of 9.518, extending 2.33 ATR below its short-term mean. The market awaits upcoming Norwegian credit and retail sales figures alongside the central bank's scheduled appearances at international policy panels.
